title: Conditional Enhancement of Dissipation-Induced Nonreciprocity by Quantum Squeezing
authors: B. -B. Liu, D. -Y. Wang, J. Tang, Gang Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, F. Nori
abstract: We systematically investigate the role of squeezing in improving dissipation-induced nonreciprocal coupling mediated by a common reservoir, by incorporating a $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinearity into either the cavity mode, the reservoir, or both. Squeezing is capable of exponentially enhancing the effective coupling, but this enhancement is not universal in such a nonreciprocal interaction. Instead, it depends on the system configuration and specific parameter regimes. Specifically, the squeezing of the reservoir injects additional energy into the system via the dissipation channel, modifying the underlying dynamics in a nontrivial manner. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances the performance of the quantum battery, including stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We provide the corresponding analytical expressions, together with a systematic analysis of energy transport and parameter optimization. Extending the framework to optical isolation, we observe an exponentially amplified output signal. Our results open a new avenue for nonreciprocal quantum information processing and nonreciprocal quantum device design.
summary: This paper theoretically explores the role of quantum squeezing in boosting dissipation-induced nonreciprocal interactions within coupled cavity systems. It demonstrates that squeezing can exponentially enhance metrics like coupling strength and energy storage in quantum batteries and optical isolators. The findings establish a tunable method for realizing enhanced, directional quantum signal processing.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum squeezing can enhance nonreciprocal coupling induced by dissipation in coupled quantum systems.
main_result: Squeezing enhances the effective coupling and improves performance metrics for quantum batteries and optical isolators, though this enhancement is highly dependent on the specific system configuration and parameter regime.
method: The analysis uses master equations and quantum Langevin equations to derive the time evolution of expectation values for coupled cavity modes interacting with a common reservoir.
model_or_system: The model involves two coupled cavity modes ($a$ and $b$) subjected to dissipation via a common reservoir, potentially incorporating $\chi^{(2)}$ nonlinearity. Squeezing is introduced into the system (cavity or reservoir) via unitary transformations.
key_observables: Effective nonreciprocal coupling strength (EC), Enhancement Effect (EE), stored energy, charging power, ergotropy, and optical transmission coefficient ($T_{ab}$).
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), coupling strength ($J$), reservoir decay rates ($\Gamma$), and detuning ($\omega_s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on solving the evolution equations for expectation values derived from the master equation in the squeezed frame.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy evolution, charging power enhancement factors, steady-state energy vs. squeezing parameter ($r$), and transmission coefficients ($T_{ab}$) showing exponential amplification with squeezing.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes five different cases based on where quantum squeezing is applied (cavity mode, reservoir, or both) to quantify its effect on nonreciprocal coupling, followed by specific applications to quantum batteries and optical isolators.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for engineering non-Hermitian effects (nonreciprocity) using non-classical resources like squeezing, which is highly relevant for designing advanced quantum optical devices.
